newsitem.title: UK: UK finance, business must prepare for EMU now - BOE.
newsitem.headline: UK finance, business must prepare for EMU now - BOE.

text.p: The British financial and business communities can and should prepare now for European Monetary Union even if Britain does not participate, Bank of England executive director Ian Plenderleith said.

If monetary union is introduced according to plan, banks and financial institutions will want to offer wholesale and international customers financial facilities in the Euro whether Britain is in or out, he told a conference.
"The preparation for wholesale business in Euro can proceed straight away...and that, indeed, is what has been happening in London at a gathering pace over the past year," he said.

As for retail business, firms need to know whether the UK is or is not joining monetary union -- scheduled to begin on January 1, 1999 -- before embarking on major changes to handle retail business in Euro, Plenderleith said.
"Euro notes and coins will not be available until 2002 and that leaves time to develop retail facilities once we know who the initial participants in EMU are," he said.
